stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan: Schools, Colleges In 6 Odisha Districts Closed Till Nov 21
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan: Schools, Colleges In 6 Odisha Districts Closed Till Nov 21
stories.summary: Collectors of all remaining districts have also been directed to monitor the local situation.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan is approaching the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha coast with winds of up to 110 kmph, prompting train rescheduling and school closures across six Odisha districts.

With winds reaching speeds of up to 100 kmph and gusts likely to touch 110 kmph, Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan is bearing down on the eastern coastline, prompting authorities in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh to step up precautionary measures.
The approaching storm has already disrupted railway schedules, while educational institutions across six Odisha districts will remain closed for three days as the state prepares for its impact.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Akvan, currently positioned over the westcentral Bay of Bengal, is likely to move north-northwestwards and cross the North Andhra Pradesh-Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri by noon on Thursday, November 19.
The system is expected to bring maximum sustained wind speeds of 90-100 kmph, with gusts reaching 110 kmph.
The approaching cyclone has prompted railway authorities to revise the departure timings of three trains scheduled to operate on Thursday.
- Train No. 18046 Charlapalli-Shalimar East Coast Express, originally scheduled to leave at 8.40 am on November 19, will now depart at 3.40 pm on the same day.
- Similarly, Train No. 12704 Secunderabad-Howrah Falaknuma Express, which was scheduled to depart at 3.55 pm, has been rescheduled to 5.55 pm.
- Train No. 15227 SMVT Bengaluru-Muzaffarpur Express will also operate behind schedule.
The train, originally scheduled to leave at 12.30 am on Thursday, will now depart at 8.30 am.

As part of its precautionary response, the Odisha government has ordered the closure of all government, government-aided and private schools, along with Anganwadi centres, in six districts from November 19 to November 21.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said the state administration was fully prepared to tackle the approaching weather system and had initiated the necessary response measures.

stories.headline: Lucknow activist demands equal opportunity in election symbols in U.P. polls
stories.title: Lucknow activist demands equal opportunity in election symbols in U.P. polls
stories.summary: The representation points out that continuity of symbols creates lasting voter familiarity and political identity, placing unrecognised parties at a structural disadvantage
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Social activist Amitabh Thakur on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) wrote to the Election Commission of India (ECI) questioning whether recognition of a political party, though a legitimate statutory status, should also confer the additional and continuing advantage of an exclusively reserved election symbol, while registered but unrecognised parties and independent candidates are denied comparable opportunities.
“In my representation to the ECI, I pointed out that continuity of symbols creates lasting voter familiarity and political identity, placing unrecognised parties at a structural disadvantage.
It is a larger constitutional issue concerning equality in symbol allotment,” told Mr. Thakur, to The Hindu, who runs Azad Adhikar Sena, a political party.
The representation points out that continuity of symbols creates lasting voter familiarity and political identity, placing unrecognised parties at a structural disadvantage.

“I proposed equal opportunity for all political parties to choose and retain common symbols under uniform rules or fresh symbol allotment to all political parties at every general election, starting with Uttar Pradesh polls.

The representation calls upon the Election Commission to examine this fundamental issue under Article 14 of the Constitution and do the needful, particularly in the context of the forthcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections,” added Mr. Thakur.

stories.headline: Election affidavit case: Tripura court directs police to book Minister Tinku Roy
stories.title: Election affidavit case: Tripura court directs police to book Minister Tinku Roy
stories.summary: Tinku Roy is accused of furnishing fake credentials in his affidavit submitted to the Election Commission
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A court in Tripura has directed the police to formally register a complaint against Tripura Minister Tinku Roy for allegedly submitting false information in his affidavit during the 2023 Assembly Elections.
The complaint was originally lodged at Kailashahar police station in Unakoti district in north Tripura, but the police did not register an FIR to initiate investigation.
Former PCC President Birajit Sinha informed that the Unakoti District and Sessions Court passed the order recently, and the same has to be proceeded with through legal formalities.
He said non-compliance on the part of the police may force them to seek further intervention of the court.

Tinku Roy was elected for the first time as MLA in 2023 from Chandipur assembly segment in Unakoti district was included in the cabinet of Dr. Manik Saha as a minister of Youth Affairs & Sports as well as a couple of other departments.
Mr. Roy, however, is accused of furnishing fake credentials in his affidavit submitted to the Election Commission.

He lied that there was no criminal case pending against him and his claim of passing higher secondary education from Gwalior-based Board of Secondary Education Madhya Bharat also not true, alleged Birajit Sinha.
Mr. Roy has not responded to the accusations, and when contacted, his office said that the Minister is busy campaigning for BJP candidates contesting elections for the Urban Local Bodies.
The elections are slated for November 27.

stories.headline: What Are Interrogatories? Explained Amid INDIA Bloc's Plea To Question Election Commission On SIR
stories.title: What Are Interrogatories? Explained Amid INDIA Bloc's Plea To Question Election Commission On SIR
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: An application moved by the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, and other INDIA bloc leaders before the Supreme Court seeking to serve 48 interrogatories on the Election Commission of India (ECI) over its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) brought into focus an important procedural mechanism under civil law.

Governed by Order XI of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC), interrogatories are a set of written questions served by one litigating party upon the opposite party, with the court's permission, to obtain answers to specific factual matters relevant to the dispute.

The purpose of serving interrogatories is to obtain admissions, clarify disputed facts, and avoid unnecessary evidence in order to narrow down the scope of the litigation, to avoid wastage of precious time and expenditure in litigation.
The interrogatories sought to be served upon the ECI seek specific factual answers concerning the ECI's decision-making process.

The questions reportedly seek particulars regarding approvals by the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, dates and modes of approval, file records, whether objections or dissent were recorded, and matters concerning electoral-roll changes and related processes.

The Supreme Court has not yet granted leave to serve interrogatories on the ECI, and has adjourned the matter till December 9, after the ECI objected to the petitioners' application, stating that a final call on the petitioner's application to serve interrogatories would be taken after hearing both sides.
What are interrogatories?
Order XI Rule 1 CPC provides that a plaintiff or defendant may, with the leave of the court, deliver interrogatories in writing for examination of the opposite party.
The provision requires interrogatories to indicate which questions each person is required to answer.
It also restricts a party from delivering more than one set of interrogatories to the same party without an order of the court.
Importantly, the questions which do not relate to matters in controversy are deemed irrelevant, even if they might otherwise be admissible during oral cross-examination.

“Provided also that interrogatories which do not relate to any matters in question in the suit shall be deemed irrelevant, notwithstanding that they might be admissible on the oral cross-examination of a witness.” the second proviso of Rule 1 says.

stories.headline: Tripura Election Commissioner Reviews Preparations for November 27 Civic Polls
stories.title: Tripura Election Commissioner Reviews Preparations for November 27 Civic Polls
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: AGARTALA: State Election Commissioner Dr Pradip Kumar Chakraborty is reviewing the preparations and visited Sipahijala District ahead of the November 27 Urban Local Body (ULB) elections in Tripura.
He stressed the need for close coordination among administrative officials, police and election authorities to ensure free, fair and peaceful polling.
A high-level review meeting was held at the conference hall of the District Magistrate and Collector's office in Bishramganj under the chairmanship of the State Election Commissioner.

The meeting was attended by Sepahijala District Magistrate and Collector-cum-District Municipal Election Officer Prashant Badal Negi, Inspector General of Police (Law and Order) Ipper Manchak, Superintendent of Police Bijoy Debbarma, election observers, Returning.
Officers (ROs), Sub-Divisional Police Officers (SDPOs), officers-in-charge of various police stations and representatives of different political parties.
During the meeting, officials reviewed the overall election arrangements, including security deployment, law and order, logistical preparedness and coordination among different departments.
Preparations for all stages of the election, including the nomination process, polling and counting, were also discussed.
Special emphasis was placed on maintaining peace in sensitive areas and preventing any untoward incidents during the election process.
The Commissioner took stock of the arrangements made by the district administration and police and stressed that all departments must work together to ensure a smooth electoral process.

stories.headline: FICCI seeks one-time power amnesty for J&K industrial units
stories.title: FICCI seeks one-time power amnesty for J&K industrial units
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 18: The Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), J&K State Council, has urged the Omar Abdullah-led government to introduce a special One-Time Power Amnesty Scheme for industrial units across Jammu and Kashmir, seeking relief from accumulated electricity liabilities that have become a financial burden for struggling businesses. In a communication addressed to Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on November 18, Rakesh Bhat, Co-Chairman, FICCI J&K State Council, said industrial establishments across the Union Territory were facing serious financial difficulties due to mounting electricity dues amid prolonged economic disruptions. The representation said the industrial sector had endured several unprecedented challenges over the years, including the COVID-19 pandemic, floods, economic disruptions and other unforeseen circumstances, adversely affecting production, business operations, cash flows and the overall financial viability of industrial units. It said a substantial number of industrial establishments had accumulated considerable outstanding electricity liabilities, making it increasingly difficult for entrepreneurs to clear dues while meeting operational expenses, employee salaries, raw material costs and other statutory obligations. Pointing out that the government had introduced power amnesty and relief schemes for different categories of electricity consumers from time to time, FICCI said the industrial sector, given its contribution to employment generation and investment, also deserved special consideration. The industry body has sought a waiver of accumulated interest, penalties and surcharge on outstanding electricity dues, along with a dedicated one-time settlement mechanism for pending liabilities. It has also proposed that eligible industrial units be allowed to clear their principal outstanding amounts through a reasonable instalment facility, besides seeking special consideration for genuinely distressed and financially affected establishments. FICCI said such a scheme would provide much-needed financial relief to industrial entrepreneurs, help revive struggling units, protect existing employment and encourage fresh investment in Jammu and Kashmir. Emphasising the importance of a financially sustainable industrial sector for the Union Territory’s economic growth, the federation urged the Chief Minister to consider the proposal favourably and take necessary steps to extend the benefits of a One-Time Power Amnesty Scheme to industrial establishments.

stories.headline: Xi, Trump and Putin meet in Shenzhen ahead of trilateral talks
stories.title: Xi, Trump and Putin meet in Shenzhen ahead of trilateral talks
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 18: Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin were pictured together in Shenzhen for the first time on Wednesday, shaking hands ahead of their much-anticipated trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. The meeting of the three leaders is being seen as a significant diplomatic moment, bringing together the heads of the world’s three major powers amid tensions over global trade, the Ukraine conflict and the war in Iran. Trump arrived in Shenzhen from the Philippines, where he attended a regional summit and met Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, among other leaders. In a departure from established diplomatic protocol, Xi personally received Trump at the airport and embraced him on the tarmac. A red carpet was rolled out for the US President. Xi has never before gone to an airport to receive a visiting American president. The BBC described the welcome as a carefully choreographed moment of flattery, reflecting the importance Beijing attaches to its relationship with Washington. The gesture also came months after Trump personally received Xi at Joint Base Andrews in the United States. Xi had earlier welcomed Putin in Shenzhen, describing the Russian President as an “old friend”. Putin’s visit, too, received a high-level reception, with Xi’s chief of staff Cai Qi welcoming him at the airport. The trilateral meeting is expected to cover a wide range of issues, including trade, denuclearisation and the Iran war. Trade tensions remain a major concern, with Trump’s tariffs disrupting global commerce and China restricting exports of critical materials, including rare earths. The existing trade truce between the two countries is due to expire in January. The leaders are also expected to discuss the nuclear issue, although China has so far been reluctant to join disarmament negotiations, citing the gap between its nuclear arsenal and those of the US and Russia. The Ukraine conflict is another major international concern, though a breakthrough is considered difficult in the absence of Ukraine’s participation in the talks. Trump has also indicated that the Iran war could figure in discussions with Xi and Putin, both of whose countries maintain strategic ties with Tehran.

stories.headline: MP Clears 200 MW Floating Solar Expansion, Taking Omkareshwar Capacity To 478 MW
stories.title: MP Clears 200 MW Floating Solar Expansion, Taking Omkareshwar Capacity To 478 MW
stories.summary: Madhya Pradesh (MP) Chief Minister (CM) Mohan Yadav, as part of a Cabinet decision, approved connectivity for a 200 MW floating solar project at the Omkareshwar Reservoir, along with a minimum 800 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) under Phase II of the project. During a media briefing on the Cabinet decisions, he said that the Cabinet had taken several far-reaching decisions on integrated industrial development, investment promotion, renewable energy, air connectivity, and administrative reforms in Madhya Pradesh. 200 MW Floating Solar Project With 800 MWh BESS For Omkareshwar Project The Cabinet approved a 200 MW floating solar project with an 800 MWh battery energy storage system under Phase II of the Omkareshwar Reservoir project. Once the 200 MW capacity under Phase II is commissioned, the combined capacity of Phase I (278 MW) and Phase II (200 MW) of the Omkareshwar Reservoir project will reach 478 MW. This makes the Omkareshwar Floating Solar Project one of the world's largest floating solar projects located on a single reservoir. The initiative aims to ensure electricity supply during peak demand hours. The project will be connected to the Inter-State Transmission System. After approval from the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, the Bid Process Coordinator will coordinate the bidding process through an open tender. First Phase Of 278 MW Omkareshwar Floating Solar Park Completed The first phase of the Omkareshwar Floating Solar Park , with a capacity of 278 MW, has been completed. It is India's largest operational floating solar project and among the largest operational projects of its kind in the world. Developed by Rewa Ultra Mega Solar Limited at a competitive tariff of ₹3.21 per kilowatt-hour, the electricity generated by the project has been procured by Madhya Pradesh Power Management Company Limited since 2024. Aligning With Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, Government of India, has announced the establishment of floating solar projects with a total capacity of 5,000 MW under the Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana, along with co-located energy storage systems providing a minimum of two hours of storage. The scheme provides for Central Financial Assistance of ₹1 crore per MW to reduce tariffs. According to the National Institute of Solar Energy's report, 'Solar PV Potential of India, June 2026' , under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, the country's total floating solar potential stands at 102.18 GW. Of this, Madhya Pradesh accounts for 14.89 GW, approximately 15 per cent of the national potential.

stories.headline: Govt performing in best capacity with no excuses, BJP attempting to weaken Govt: CM
stories.title: Govt performing in best capacity with no excuses, BJP attempting to weaken Govt: CM
stories.summary: Rajouri, Nov 18: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday said that government was performing in best capacity with no member of government giving a coward excuse of being a UT government and promises made in the election manifesto were being fulfilled. In his statement during rally, CM Omar said that Bhartiya Janta Party (BJP) was leaving no stone upturned in demeaning the J&K government and humiliating it but ground reality was that their government was working in the best manner and was also fulfilling its promises. "We have given six free cylinders, have given relief in the form of 200 free electricity units through solar, hiked social welfare pensions as well as monetary aid for marriage assistance scheme, provided free travel for women in government buses," he said stressing that all the promises made in the election manifesto would be fulfilled. "The main thing is that we are part of UT with limited resources but none of my colleage ever gave an excuse of it as we are not cowards," the CM said. Accusing BJP of attempting to humilate the J&K government, he questioned difference in protocol positions of elected representatives in Warrant of Precedence of a state and UT. "If a Chief Secretary and a High Court Chief Justice enjoys same position in Warrant of Precedence of a state as well as a UT, then why is there sharp difference between positions of elected representatives," CM Omar said. He also talked about resumption of Darbar Move practice in Jammu and Kashmir to benefit economy of Jammu province as well as shifting examination pattern of Kashmir winter areas to October-November session. "We even followed the project of Mughal Road tunnel in best possible manner and our colleagues including Deputy CM Surinder Choudhary remained in contact with Delhi and it is a result of our efforts that the DPR making is in process and will be approved soon and you will see work on it after which round the year traffic movement will be possible," the CM said. Addressing the public rally in Mendhar, he accused the Centre of not taking any solid step regarding reservation matter of J&K despite submission of cabinet committee reports multiple times. "The report of our cabinet committee on reservation was submitted at appropriate quarters. However, as we are a UT, the report was returned to us with some objections which we covered. This has happened multiple times. We are submitting reports and they return with objections. We reply to objections and then a new query is put. This all is being done only to stall a solution," CM Omar said.

stories.headline: Mughal road tunnel work to commence soon: CM
stories.title: Mughal road tunnel work to commence soon: CM
stories.summary: Mendhar (Poonch), Nov 18: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday stated that the work on the Mughal road tunnel would commence very soon and in the coming years, the road would remain open throughout the year, ensuring all-weather connectivity between the two regions. He said that providing all-weather connectivity between the Pir Panjal region and Kashmir through the historic Mughal road was the dream of former Chief Minister Sher-e-Kashmir Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah. He was addressing the gathering after dedicating 13 development projects worth Rs 92.84 Cr to the people of Mendhar in the frontier district of Poonch, giving fresh impetus to infrastructure development and strengthening essential public services in the border constituency. The projects, spread across road connectivity, power infrastructure, flood protection, education and drinking water supply, include eight inaugurations and five foundation stone-laying ceremonies, reflecting the government’s continued focus on improving basic amenities and extending development to remote and border areas. Addressing a large public gathering, the Chief Minister highlighted the key initiatives undertaken by the government to fulfil its commitments to the people, particularly in social welfare, public transport, education, recruitment and restoration of the Darbar Move. He reiterated that the restoration of statehood to Jammu and Kashmir remained a key commitment, saying he had consistently reminded the Prime Minister and Union Home Minister of the assurance made to the people, both during their visits to Jammu and Kashmir and in meetings in Delhi. Highlighting the implementation of welfare commitments, Omar Abdullah said the government had initiated the provision of six free LPG cylinders annually to the poorest households, as part of its promise of 12 cylinders. He also referred to the progress made towards providing 200 units of free electricity through solar energy. Emphasising measures aimed at easing the financial burden on women, he said free travel in government buses had been introduced for women, particularly benefiting students commuting to schools and colleges. The government had also enhanced social security benefits, including old-age and widow pensions, besides increasing marriage assistance for economically weaker families. On employment and reservation, the Chief Minister said the government had taken up recruitment-related commitments and constituted a Cabinet Sub-Committee to examine reservation-related issues and address concerns in this regard. Among the major projects, the Chief Minister laid the foundation stone for a 50 MVA, 132/33 KV Grid Sub-Station at Mendhar, being executed by JKP
